items.stem: Under the FLSA, a non-exempt employee works 46 hours in a workweek. How are the extra hours generally compensated?

options.text: At one-and-one-half times the regular rate for hours over 40
options.rationale: Correct: non-exempt employees receive at least 1.5x the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek.

options.text: At the regular rate with no premium
options.rationale: Hours over 40 for non-exempt workers require an overtime premium.

options.text: At double the regular rate for all 46 hours
options.rationale: Overtime applies only to hours over 40, and the FLSA minimum premium is 1.5x, not 2x.

options.text: Not at all, because salaried rules apply
options.rationale: The employee is non-exempt, so salaried-exempt rules do not apply.

items.explanation: Correct: non-exempt employees receive at least 1.5x the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek.

items.stem: When computing taxable wages, how are qualifying pre-tax (Section 125) deductions treated?

options.text: Subtracted from gross pay before income tax is withheld
options.rationale: Correct: qualifying pre-tax deductions reduce the wage base before applicable taxes are calculated.

options.text: Added to gross pay before tax is withheld
options.rationale: Deductions reduce, not increase, the wage base.

options.text: Withheld only after net pay is calculated
options.rationale: Pre-tax deductions apply before tax calculation, not after net pay.
They are not ignored; they specifically reduce taxable wages.

items.explanation: Correct: qualifying pre-tax deductions reduce the wage base before applicable taxes are calculated.

items.stem: Select TWO factors that typically indicate a worker should be classified as an employee rather than an independent contractor.

options.text: The business controls how and when the work is performed
options.rationale: Correct: behavioural control over how/when work is done points to employee status.

options.text: The worker is economically dependent on the business for ongoing work
options.rationale: Correct: economic dependence and an ongoing relationship point to employee status.

options.text: The worker offers services to the general public and has multiple clients
options.rationale: Serving many clients points toward independent-contractor status.

options.text: The worker supplies their own tools and bears profit/loss risk
options.rationale: Bearing business risk and supplying tools points toward contractor status.

options.text: The worker sets their own business insurance and files as a business
options.rationale: Operating as an independent business points toward contractor status.

items.explanation: Correct: behavioural control over how/when work is done points to employee status.
